Hi Olga / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the execs liked the latency profile and the cost projections. As we discussed, procurement wants a concise mutual action plan so we can sign off quickly and spin up our POC environment. High-level asks from our side:

- Org setup and sandbox API keys for testing (non-prod)
- IP allowlist (we will provide ranges)
- VPC peering from our AWS account into Redwood Private test VPC
- Expected maintenance / downtime window during peering

I've attached our initial MAP spreadsheet (mediocore_map_v1.xlsx) and a POA for procurement. Can you confirm Redwood's owner for each line item and give an estimate for completion (we're aiming to go-live with the POC by 2026-12-10)?

Emily, thanks — clear ask. We'll own the following from Redwood:

1) Create a Redwood sandbox org and generate scoped API keys for your test users (delivery ETA: 2026-12-03 EOD)
2) Provide a formal IP allowlist template; we'll need the exact public CIDR(s) you want whitelisted (ETA: template by 2026-12-02)
3) Coordinate VPC peering — we can peer with your AWS account (we'll need the account ID and preferred AZs). Planning note: peering itself is non-disruptive; routing changes are self-contained.
4) Canary plan: small traffic roll for first 48 hours then full ramp.

I've attached our VPC peering template (vpc_peering_template.yaml) for your infra team to review. Next immediate asks for your side so we keep to the 12/10 target:
- Confirm the AWS account ID to peer with
- Provide public IP ranges (or NAT IPs) for API allowlist
- Sign the POA and return (procurement)

Rishi will run the on-call integration for API keys and vaulting; Vivek will own the peering and routing. Laura will help with the paperwork and DocuSign streamlining.

Proposed milestone dates:
- 12/02: IP allowlist template and peering template delivered (done)
- 12/03: Redwood sandbox org + test API keys issued
- 12/04: VPC peering handshake and connectivity checks
- 12/05–12/06: Canary traffic and performance checks
- 12/09: Final sign-off prep
- 12/10: POC acceptance

If that schedule works, we'll generate the keys and open a temporary support channel for the POC.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Emily — quick technical notes from Redwood SRE/SE: 

- For the API keys we'll generate two scoped keys (test and load) with expiration set to 90 days. Please confirm the list of test user emails that should be allowed to mint tokens from your side so we can bind them to the keys.
- For IP allowlist: we support CIDR ranges and single IPs. If your infra sits behind a NAT pool, please provide the NAT egress IPs rather than internal subnets. Example format: 52.23.112.0/24; 203.0.113.45/32.
- VPC peering: we require your AWS account ID and the VPC id for peering (we will create the peering connection on Redwood's side once we have those). If you prefer cross-account role-based setup for automation, share the role ARN.

Two clarifying Qs:
1) Do you have a preference for whether the test API keys are placed in your org-level vault or in Redwood's managed sandbox? (we recommend Redwood-managed for faster onboarding)
2) Any compliance constraints on token logging or metrics retention for the POC?

I'll stand up the sandbox once Olga confirms scope.

- Rishi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Emily / Procurement,

Great — thanks for the prompt responses and the AWS details. Short answers to your remaining concerns:

- Peering impact: Peering itself does not cause host-level downtime; routing changes are additive. If your team configures route propagation on their side immediately after the peering acceptance, we expect negligible disruption (near-zero maintenance window). If you want an absolutely silent flip, schedule the final route adds during an agreed quiet hour; we can do a canary flow to validate.

- Keys & logging: We'll place the sandbox keys in Redwood-managed vaults and scope them to the two test users you listed. For the POC, logs will be kept in Redwood for 7 days and not forwarded to external SIEMs. We'll provide a short retention policy doc.

Confirmed schedule (updated):
- 12/03: Sandbox org + test API keys (COMPLETE)
- 12/04: Peering connection initiated and connectivity tests (COMPLETE)
- 12/05: Canary traffic + performance checks (in progress)
- 12/07: Final acceptance sign-off (tentative)

Next steps for procurement: once we have the signed POA and DocuSign back, Laura will submit the internal activation ticket and we will start the formal POC kickoff call. I've uploaded the signed POA placeholder to the Drive link and added a DocuSign link for final signature: https://app.docusign.com/XXX-DocuSign-Link

Checklist (we will tick these as we close):
- [ ] POA signed by MediCore procurement
- [ ] IP allowlist confirmed in Redwood sandbox
- [ ] Canary run completed with <5% error rate
- [ ] Performance baseline documented and shared

If procurement sends the signed POA today, we can keep the 12/07 sign-off target. I'll open a dedicated Slack channel and invite Emily and MediCore infra for live troubleshooting during the canary.
